{"self_assessment":"Impact: I took ownership of the bottom line of the fish body and had it laid and connected early (done by about 2:30), which gave the table a full lower outline from the tail point round to the nose. I then picked up the lower tail lobe (stroke 6) and laid it from the body, and stood a fallen domino back up in it. The final body, both tail lobes and the fin fell with the start, and the fish was recognizable.

Execution: I worked in steady tracing runs on the bottom curve, then inspected the area closely several times to check the joints, including the lower tail joint near the body. When Tom's fin had a jammed domino, I looked at it and pointed out where the break was and a way to fix it. After that I kept my hands off the body so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work clearly with Leo, Tom and Priya: I took the bottom line and lower tail lobe, Leo had the upper lobe, and Tom had the fin. I asked Tom to stay on the top or help with the tail so we weren't crowding each other, and I kept clear of other people's areas. I confirmed hands-off with the group before the push.

Leadership: I claimed work early, said plainly what I was doing, and reduced overlap by redirecting help to where it was needed. I held back from extra touching during the last minutes to protect a connected picture. I think my part, the bottom outline and lower tail, was a substantial piece of the result, though the picture was a real team effort.","my_share_percent":30}
